title: Control plane — Audit sampling and signed approval artifacts (PRD notes)
content:
Goal and context:
This note captures a pragmatic PRD-level approach for how the control plane will: (a) sample and persist audit evidence for customer-managed network changes and approval gates, (b) produce cryptographically verifiable approval artifacts that an auditor or customer can fetch, and (c) maintain a bounded, searchable retention store suitable for compliance reviews. This differs from the prior network-focused PRDs by focusing on sampling strategy, signed proof-of-approval, and a retrieval UX/contract for customers and auditors.

Why this matters:
- Customers in regulated environments sometimes cannot or will not ship full packet-level network logs to Redwood. We need an evidence model that: minimal surface area, provable authenticity, queryable, and exportable.
- Existing PRDs assume full immutable event captures. That is expensive and may expose PII. Sampling + signatures reduces cost and risk while providing auditability.

Key concepts / definitions:
- Evidence bundle: an immutable, ZIP-like object containing the minimal artefacts needed to reconstruct the change: approval metadata, change diff, hashed network config snapshot, requester identity, timestamp, and signatures.
- Signed approval token (SAT): a short base64 string produced by Redwood when an approval gate completes; it encodes a compact hash and a Redwood signature. Optionally co-signed by a customer-managed key (KMSEncrypt) when configured.
- Sampling window: configurable TTL-based window that determines which changes are persisted as full evidence bundles vs. minimal indexed records.

High-level requirements (MUST/MAY):
MUST: Create an evidence bundle for any approval gate that affects customer-managed networking (VPC peering, route-table change, IP allowlist update) when the change state is one of: approved, rejected, escalated-to-legal.
MUST: Issue a SAT at approval time and return it to the caller (API response and UI).
MUST: Support customer-managed signing: when customer enables "co-signing", Redwood will accept a customer signature (JWK or PKCS#11 handshake) and include it in the bundle.
MUST: Provide an API to fetch an evidence bundle by SAT with RBAC checks (customer-admin and Redwood-audit roles).
MUST: Maintain an index of events that supports queries by date range, approver, SAT, ticket id.
MAY: For high-volume tenants, allow sample_rate override where only 1 in N changes store the full bundle; all changes still get an indexed record and SAT.

Sampling & retention policy (proposal):
- Default: 100% of changes for tier Enterprise/Private keep full evidence for 365 days; for SMB tiers store full evidence for 30 days then compress to a compact index entry for 365 days total retention.
- Sampling controls: project-level policy: {"mode": "full|sample|minimal", "sample_ratio": "1/N"}. (UI exposes slider and REST field sample_ratio).
- Compact index entry fields (kept forever or customer-defined): sat, change_type, change_hash, actor_id, timestamp, ticket_ref, short_summary, encryption_key_id.
- Evidence bundles are stored encrypted-at-rest with Redwood key; if co-signed, customer may optionally request their own copy be pushed to an S3/GCS path they control (customer export).

Evidence bundle schema (human readable example):
- sat: base64...
- change_id: redwood-change-2024-...
- change_type: route-table-update
- actor: rina.shah@redwood.ai
- timestamp: 2024-11-05T16:32:12Z
- ticket: JIRA-1234
- diff: (text)
- config_snapshot_hash: sha256:abc123
- redwood_signature: base64sig
- customer_signature: base64sig (optional)
- proof_manifest: [file list + checksums]

APIs and UX:
- POST /controlplane/changes (existing) -> returns sat in response when gate resolves. Include header X-Redwood-Evidence: SAT.
- GET /controlplane/evidence/{sat} -> returns signed evidence bundle.  Auth: customer-admin or audit role, with support for short-lived presigned URLs for external auditors.
- UI: Evidence tab on change detail page showing SAT, integrity verified status (green if signatures valid), download bundle button, and export-to-customer-bucket action.

Cryptographic considerations:
- Redwood uses ECDSA-P256 to sign SATs; signatures include timestamp and change_hash to prevent replay.
- Customer co-signing uses one of: JWK public key registration, PKCS#11 HSM handshake, or an automated upload of a CSR + cert. For the first phase, support JWK.
- SAT verification: a legal auditor should be able to verify that a given SAT was issued by Redwood by fetching the public verification keys from a stable JWKS endpoint and validating the signed payload.

Operational concerns and SRE bounds:
- Evidence generation is async but must be available within 30s for the GET API (SLO: 95% within 30s).
- Storage cost optimized by compression and by enabling customer export+delete triggers (customer can request copy and Redwood will delete after copy success within N hours).
- Index must support paginated scans for audit exports; avoid full-table scans for tenant-scoped queries.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should every rejected change generate a full bundle by default? (cost vs. compliance)
- Default retention for regulated tenants (HIPAA/PCI) — 365 vs. configurable to 7 years?
- Legal acceptability of SAT as "proof" in foreign jurisdictions. Need compliance/legal review.
- UX for co-signing: how to surface key rotation and invalidation to avoid stale proofs.

Failure modes and mitigation:
- Customer refuses co-sign request -> Redwood still signs and retains the bundle, mark "customer_signature": null but persist proof_manifest.
- Signature verification fails on fetch -> present both raw bundle and verification errors; record a forensics ticket and escalate to SRE.
- Export to customer-bucket fails -> retry with exponential backoff and notify customer with coherent error and troubleshooting steps.

Migration notes / interactions with other PRDs:
- Intersects with private-deployments/network-onboarding PRD: evidence capture should hook into onboarding pipelines to capture initial baseline snapshot.
- Should reuse the existing control-plane audit index (avoid separate store) but add columns for SAT and co-sign status.

Acceptance criteria (for implementation sprint):
1) SAT returned in API responses for approvals (unit tests covering edge cases).
2) GET evidence by SAT returns signed bundle (integration test: verification via JWKS).
3) UI shows evidence tab with valid/invalid signature state and download/export buttons.
4) Sample rate policy applies and preserves index-only entries at correct ratio.
5) Docs: public API docs and an internal playbook for SRE on signature failures.

Next steps / action items:
- (Aisha) Draft API contract and sample responses (due 2024-08-28) — PRD->API owner handoff.
- (Miguel) Spike on customer co-signing JWK flow and simulate key rotations (due 2024-09-04).
- (Rina) Compliance check on SAT legal standing + retention defaults (due 2024-09-11).
- (Evan) Storage cost estimate for 30/365 day retention scenarios (due 2024-09-01).

Notes to reviewers:
This is intentionally a pragmatic proposal to balance cost and auditability. The heart of the design is: (1) keep an immutable compact index for all changes, (2) optionally store full evidence bundles with strong signatures, and (3) provide customer export and co-signing for maximum trust. Feedback requested on sampling defaults, retention defaults for regulated tenants, and whether SAT should be long-lived (opaque) or revocable (introduce revocation list).

Attachments / references (in-drive):
- link to onboarding-runbook draft: CONFLUENCE-PLATFORM-1234
- spike notes: /shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/signature-spike-notes (TBD)

End of PRD notes.
